title: Privileged access audit and escalation runbook
content:
Purpose:
This runbook documents the on-call triage, containment, evidence collection, and post-incident steps specific to suspected privileged access abuse (compromised user/service account, sudden role grants, or API key exfiltration). It covers practical SIEM queries, audit log fields we must capture, automated evidence export checkpoints, and escalation contacts.

Scope:
- Applies to incidents where a privileged principal (user/service account, API key, service token) performs anomalous actions or where RBAC v2 grants are observed outside expected change windows.
- Environments: hosted API, dedicated clusters, private deployments (VPC), cloud control planes (GCP/AWS/Azure).
- Not intended for pure application bugs or non-privileged data-only incidents (use app incident runbooks).

Quick summary (TL;DR):
1) If on-call sees suspicious privileged activity, immediately: isolate credentials (revoke/rotate), snapshot audit logs, notify SRE/Security lead.
2) Run SIEM queries (examples below) to scope blast radius.
3) Collect evidence via automated export (S3/GCS) and create an evidence ledger entry.
4) Contain: revoke sessions and temporary grants, enforce fallback model.
5) Post-incident: run blameless postmortem using template below, adjust RBAC policies and harden automation.

Roles and contacts:
- Primary on-call (security): see on-call rota page (linked).
- Secondary escalation: Marcus Chen (eng-sre).
- Incident commander (if Sev2+): Ellen Rivera (security manager).
- Legal/privacy: Samir Kapoor (counsel) for PII/notification guidance.
- Pager/Slack channel: #sec-oncall and #incidents.

Detection triggers (examples):
- New role grant created with admin privileges outside scheduled maintenance window.
- Service account key creation for a sensitive SA with immediate data exfil patterns.
- JWT or API key used from a new geolocation or AS number with high request volume.
- High-rate invocation of management APIs (iam.*, gsutil cp, aws s3 cp to external hosts).
- Multiple failed MFA attempts followed by successful privileged actions.

Initial triage checklist (first 15 minutes):
- Confirm alert legitimacy (false positives: automation runs, CI jobs, scheduled ops). Check associated runbooks/PR numbers.
- Identify principal (user/service): extract principal id from audit logs. Field names (see Audit Log Schema below).
- Snapshot relevant audit logs (last 24h by default): query and export.
- If credential compromise suspected: rotate/revoke keys, disable sessions (see Containment).
- Open incident in tracker and set severity. Add initial notes and evidence pointers.
- Notify stakeholders per severity matrix.

Containment steps (immediate):
1) Revoke/rotate:
   - GCP: gcloud iam service-accounts keys delete <KEY_ID> --iam-account=<SA>@<PROJECT>.iam.gserviceaccount.com
   - AWS: aws iam delete-access-key --user-name <USER> --access-key-id <AKID> or disable role sessions via sts:RevokeSession (if using AWS SSO/custom).
   - Azure: az ad app credential delete --id <appId> --key-id <keyId> or disable service principal.
   - Hosted API tokens: rotate token via admin console, add temporary deny-list rule for token id.
2) Revoke active sessions: rotate SSO sessions or set session policy to deny for the principal.
3) Lock down RBAC: remove recently added grants (if safe), or move principal to a quarantine group with no admin privileges.
4) Add additional logging hooks (increase audit retention for affected resources).
5) If exfil suspected, block egress to untrusted destinations at network layer while preserving evidence.

Audit log schema (fields to capture for every event):
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- principal_type (user|service_account|api_key|token)
- principal_id (email/service-account-id/hash)
- action (API method / syscall / operation)
- resource (full resource path, e.g., projects/prod-billing/instances/...)
- old_role / new_role (for IAM role changes)
- ip_address
- user_agent
- request_id / trace_id
- outcome (success|failure|denied)
- raw_payload (base64 or gzipped JSON blob)
- retention_bucket_uri (where the exported evidence lives)
Example (single-line):
2025-02-18T13:17:04Z | service_account | infra-deployer@prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com | iam.serviceAccounts.keys.create | projects/redwood-prod/serviceAccounts/infra-deployer@... | old_role=svc_deployer new_role=svc_deployer | 3.88.12.23 | gcloud/367.0 | req-12345 | success | gs://sec-evidence/2025-02-18/req-12345.json.gz

SIEM queries (examples) - adapt to Splunk/Chronicle/Elastic:
- New admin role grant in last 1h:
  index=redwood_audit action=IAM_ROLE_GRANT earliest=-1h | stats count by principal_id, new_role | where new_role="admin"
- Service account key creation + external network dst within 10m:
  (action=iam.serviceAccounts.keys.create) OR (dest.ip!=internal_cidr AND action=network.egress) | transaction request_id maxspan=10m
- Unusual token usage: detect token used from >3 distinct countries within 24h:
  index=auth_logs principal_type=token | iplocation ip_address | stats dc(country) as countries by principal_id | where countries>3
- Bulk object read from sensitive bucket:
  index=storage access_type=read bucket=sensitive-prod | stats sum(bytes) by principal_id, dest_ip | where sum(bytes) > 100000000

Evidence automation/export checklist:
- For the incident scope, export: audit logs (admin, auth, storage), network flow logs (VPC flow / flow logs), host process snapshots (where applicable), and object access logs.
- Use automated playbooks: (script) sec-exports/run-evidence-export.sh --incident=<INC> --resources="list" --dest=gs://sec-evidence/<INC>/
- Ensure consistent naming: <INC>-<resource>-<utc-timestamp>.json.gz
- Hash each exported artifact (sha256) and store hash in evidence ledger with timestamp and exporter id.
- Retention: immediate snapshot kept 90 days in high-availability bucket; move to cold storage after 90 days unless requested by Legal.

Containment verification (after actions):
- Verify revoked keys no longer appear in logs for new API calls.
- Confirm no new role grants for the principal.
- Re-run SIEM queries to ensure activity falls to baseline.
- Document confirmations in incident ticket.

Forensics notes (quick):
- If host-level compromise suspected, coordinate with SRE for live memory capture snapshot (only with approved process).
- Preserve disk images where required; involve legal before sharing externally.
- Do not power-cycle critical VMs unless instructed by incident commander.

RBAC v2-specific considerations:
- RBAC v2 supports ephemeral grants and just-in-time elevation. Check audit fields for grant_lifetime, requestor_id, and approval_flow_id.
- Ephemeral tokens should be invalidated by revoking the approval_flow_id or invalidating the authorizer service.
- When rolling back a grant, ensure that downstream derived rolebindings (group membership changes, rolebindings in namespace) are also examined.

Post-incident (24–72h) actions and postmortem template (blameless):
- Timeline: reconstruction with timestamps and evidence pointers.
- Root cause: succinct sentence + technical details.
- Detection gap: how did alert fire (or why not).
- Containment effectiveness: what worked, what didn't.
- Remediation & hardening: concrete items (e.g., require approval for admin grants, reduce default token lifetime, add specific SIEM rules).
- Owner & ETA for each remediation action.
- Communication notes: who was notified, customer impact, legal actions.
- Lessons learned and process changes (update this runbook).

Sample incident timeline entry (example):
- 2025-02-18T13:12Z: SIEM alert: sudden admin grant (rule id: RBAC_ADMIN_GRANT_1). link to event req-12345.
- 13:15Z: on-call confirmed non-scheduled change, rotated SA keys for infra-deployer. exported audit logs to gs://sec-evidence/INC-20250218-01/
- 13:40Z: blocked egress to external S3 endpoints at network firewall.
- 14:05Z: identified lateral activity from compromised token; disabled token, engaged SRE for host snapshot.

Postmortem checklist (immediate):
- Draft postmortem within 48h, circulate to stakeholders.
- Publish final postmortem after remediation verification.

Notes to self / unresolved items (working):
- Add concrete support for Chronicle query language (TODO: Samir to add examples).
- Verify automation script permission boundaries (least privilege) — PR referenced above.
- Decide whether to redact user emails in public postmortems (legal input required).

Appendix: Quick Slack text templates (use for initial comms)
- To #sec-oncall (short): "[INC-2025-02-18-01] Possible privileged compromise: admin grant observed for infra-deployer@prod. Keys rotated, evidence exported to gs://sec-evidence/INC-20250218-01. On-call: @MarcusChen please join."
- Pager to incident commander (detailed): include incident id, affected resources, immediate actions taken, link to evidence bucket, severity.

Revision history:
- 2024-11-02: created by Aisha Patel (initial draft)
- 2025-02-19: added SIEM query examples and sample timeline (Ellen Rivera)
- 2025-12-08: updated RBAC v2 ephemeral grant instructions and evidence retention (Marcus Chen)

End of document.
